subtitulo: Margin, stock and cash flow for an apparel brand
excerpt: We turned an operation under pressure from overstock, unclear margins and cash constraints into a business with positive, stable cash flow. By measuring real profitability by SKU, channel and promotion, the brand could decide what to sell, when to promote and how to protect cash.
contexto: The company is an apparel retail brand selling directly to consumers, with strong dependence on promotional campaigns and a cost structure sensitive to customer acquisition costs, payment fees and shipping logistics.
problema: After a critical liquidity episode caused by overstock, the company did not have enough funds for advertising, operating payments and broader commitments. Although sales grew in certain periods, customer acquisition costs, shipping costs and payment-management commissions compressed margins until cash flows became tight and weakly profitable.
solucion: We implemented margin visibility by SKU, category, channel and promotional campaign. Pricing, stock planning and product-promotion criteria were redefined by incorporating full acquisition, payment and logistics costs to estimate the real profitability of each commercial decision.
resultado: The brand achieved positive and stable cash flow, reducing its dependence on seasonal cycles and aggressive promotions. Margins doubled through better SKU promotion choices, pricing adjustments and stock planning aligned with real profitability and cash needs.

subtitulo: Operational data to improve cash, incentives and expansion
excerpt: We centralized operational and financial information from a service-station network into a database with dashboards, reports and actionable metrics. This improved daily management, aligned commercial incentives with cash and profitability goals, and freed management for strategic decisions.
contexto: The company operates several service stations with multiple business units, high transaction frequency and a need for daily decisions around sales, suppliers, cash, inventory and commercial incentives.
problema: Operational information was fragmented and there was no integrated view of key metrics for short-term decision-making. This made it difficult to anticipate cash needs, negotiate with suppliers, assess the profitability of each business unit and align sales incentives with internal financial goals.
solucion: We designed an operational database and a system of dashboards, reports and metrics for daily management. The indicators were built to monitor sales, margins, cash, suppliers, business-unit performance and commercial incentives, with a focus on short-term decisions and financial control.
resultado: The company improved its financial position with suppliers and aligned sales incentives with cash needs and internal profitability goals. Management and middle office teams were also able to focus on more strategic tasks, such as reviewing each business unit and analyzing organic and external investment opportunities for expansion.

subtitulo: Information, processes and structure for a family-owned SME
excerpt: We centralized the information flow of a family-owned SME with three business units into a quasi-accounting system. With economic and financial visibility, the company redesigned processes, professionalized responsibilities and freed management to focus on strategy, suppliers and investing excess cash.
contexto: The company is a family-owned SME with three different business units, historically operated through decentralized processes, scattered information and heavy management involvement in low-scale daily tasks.
problema: The lack of integrated information prevented the company from properly assessing the economic and financial performance of each business unit. Management was absorbed by daily operational tasks, limiting its ability to negotiate with suppliers, rethink strategy, organize internal responsibilities and decide how to invest excess cash.
solucion: We centralized information in a single quasi-accounting system, structuring economic and financial performance reports by business unit. With that visibility, operating flows were redesigned, responsibilities were reassigned, employees were trained in the new processes and incentives were aligned with business goals.
resultado: The company transformed its operation through small organizational changes with high impact: clearer responsibilities, team upskilling and less dependence on management in daily operations. This made it possible to focus on supplier negotiation, corporate strategy and investing excess cash in financial and physical assets, diversifying income from operating assets toward more passive assets.
